The
Wise
Soldier
and
the
Secret
Kingdom
Once
upon
a
time,
a
soldier
and
a
huntsman
set
out
on
a
journey
together. As
night
fell,
they
sought
shelter
in
a
house
near
the
forest. An
old
woman
warned
them
that
it
was
a
den
for
robbers. Soon
enough,
the
robbers
returned,
and
the
old
woman's
warning
came
true. The
robbers
captured
the
soldier
and
the
huntsman.

Quick
thinking,
the
soldier
came
up
with
a
plan. He
told
the
robbers
they
were
hungry
and
thirsty
and
asked
for
some
food
and
drink
before
anything
else. The
robbers
agreed,
and
while
they
were
busy
eating
and
drinking,
the
soldier
secretly
cast
a
spell
on
them. Suddenly,
the
robbers
found
themselves
unable
to
move! Seizing
the
opportunity,
the
soldier
and
the
huntsman,
along
with
some
friends
of
the
huntsman,
arrested
the
robbers. Together,
they
took
the
captured
robbers
to
a
nearby
kingdom.

It
turned
out
that
the
huntsman
was
not
just
an
ordinary
huntsman;
he
was
the
king
in
disguise! The
people
in
the
kingdom
had
been
scared
of
the
robbers,
but
they
couldn't
catch
them. So,
the
king
took
matters
into
his
own
hands. Grateful
for
the
soldier's
help,
the
king
invited
him
to
live
in
the
kingdom. The
king
promised
to
provide
everything
the
soldier
needed,
and
from
that
day
on,
the
soldier
happily
lived
in
the
kingdom,
where
he
had
all
his
needs
taken
care
of. Moral:
Teamwork
and
clever
thinking
can
overcome
challenges,
leading
to
success
and
happiness.

The
Wishing
Cap
and
the
Crystal
Ball
Once
upon
a
time,
there
was
a
sorceress
who
had
three
sons. One
day,
she
used
her
magic
to
turn
two
of
her
sons
into
an
eagle
and
a
whale. But
the
third
son
was
smart. He
ran
away
to
escape
his
mother's
spell. As
he
journeyed,
he
stumbled
upon
two
giants
arguing
over
a
magical
wishing
cap. Quick
as
a
wink,
he
grabbed
the
cap
and
wished
himself
into
a
castle. Inside,
he
met
a
kind
princess
who
told
him
about
a
crystal
ball
that
could
break
the
spell
on
his
brothers.

To
find
the
crystal
ball,
the
princess
gave
him
a
special
task. He
had
to
fight
a
fierce
bull
near
a
spring. When
he
defeated
the
bull,
a
bird
flew
out
of
it. This
bird
laid
an
egg,
and
inside
the
yolk
of
that
egg
was
a
precious
crystal
ball. But
there
was
a
catch! The
princess
warned
him
that
if
he
dropped
the
egg,
everything
would
be
destroyed
by
fire. Determined
to
save
his
brothers,
the
young
boy
followed
her
instructions
carefully
and
retrieved
the
crystal
ball.

As
soon
as
he
broke
the
spell
with
the
crystal
ball,
his
brothers
returned
to
their
human
forms. Grateful
for
his
bravery
and
kindness,
the
princess
married
the
youngest
son,
and
they
lived
happily
ever
after. Moral:
Courage
and
determination
can
overcome
even
the
most
powerful
magic,
and
kindness
is
rewarded
with
love
and
happiness. The
Glass
Mountain's
Secret
Once
upon
a
time,
there
was
a
king
who
built
a
tall
glass
mountain. He
declared,
"Whoever
can
climb
this
mountain
can
marry
my
daughter!"

The
princess
wanted
to
help
one
of
the
suitors,
so
she
joined
him
in
climbing
the
mountain. But,
oh
no!
As
they
climbed,
the
princess
slipped
and
fell,
and
the
mountain
swallowed
her
up! Inside
the
mountain,
she
met
Old
Rinkrank,
a
wizard. He
made
her
work
for
him
as
his
servant. Every
day,
he
would
magically
bring
out
a
ladder
from
his
pocket,
climb
up
the
mountain,
and
then
pull
the
ladder
back
up
with
him. When
he
returned,
he
would
bring
gold
and
silver
with
him. One
day,
the
princess
had
an
idea.

She
closed
all
the
doors
and
windows
of
the
cave,
leaving
only
a
tiny
window
open. When
Rinkrank
returned,
she
refused
to
open
the
door. Instead,
she
peeked
out
through
the
small
window
and
saw
Rinkrank's
long
beard. Quickly,
she
slammed
the
window
shut
on
his
beard,
trapping
him! With
Rinkrank
stuck,
the
princess
was
free
to
climb
out
using
the
ladder. She
rushed
to
her
father
and
told
him
everything
that
had
happened. The
king
was
furious
with
Rinkrank
for
trapping
his
daughter,
so
he
punished
the
wizard.

Finally,
the
princess
was
able
to
marry
the
suitor
she
had
helped,
and
they
lived
happily
ever
after. Moral:
Cleverness
and
courage
can
overcome
challenges,
and
kindness
is
rewarded
in
the
end. The
Traveller
and
the
Tears
of
Emerald
Once
upon
a
time,
a
kind
old
woman
met
a
traveller. She
had
a
heavy
bag
and
asked
the
traveller
for
help
to
carry
it
up
the
mountain. Together,
they
climbed
and
climbed
until
they
reached
the
mountain's
top. There,
they
saw
a
girl
taking
care
of
geese.

The
old
woman
was
grateful
for
the
traveller's
help,
so
she
gave
him
a
special
box
filled
with
shiny
emeralds. The
traveller
said
his
goodbyes
and
continued
his
journey. As
he
traveled,
he
reached
a
kingdom. Curious
about
what
was
inside
the
box,
he
went
to
the
king
and
presented
the
emeralds. When
the
queen
saw
them,
she
gasped
and
told
the
traveller
a
surprising
story. She
explained
that
her
daughter's
tears
turned
into
emeralds. The
king
had
sent
her
away
from
the
kingdom
for
something
she
did
wrong,
but
now
he
regretted
his
decision.

The
traveller
shared
the
story
and
revealed
where
he
got
the
box. Together,
they
all
went
back
to
the
mountain. As
they
reached
the
top,
they
were
filled
with
joy
and
sadness. The
old
woman
disappeared,
and
the
king
and
queen
cried
when
they
saw
their
daughter
tending
geese. The
wise
old
woman
reappeared
and
scolded
the
king
and
queen,
telling
them
they
had
been
unfair
to
their
daughter. Then,
like
magic,
the
family
was
reunited. They
hugged
each
other
tightly,
grateful
to
be
together
again. And
from
that
day
on,
they
lived
happily
ever
after.

Moral:
Never
judge
someone
too
quickly,
for
they
may
be
more
precious
than
you
realize. The
Woodcutter's
Daughter
and
the
Kindness
Spell
Once
upon
a
time,
there
was
a
woodcutter
with
three
daughters. One
day,
he
asked
his
eldest
daughter
to
bring
him
food
in
the
woods. But,
oh
dear,
she
lost
her
way
and
found
herself
in
front
of
a
hut. Inside,
there
was
an
old
man,
a
hen,
a
cock,
and
a
cow. The
old
man
kindly
let

her
stay
and
she
cooked
dinner
for
everyone.

As
night
fell,
the
old
man
opened
a
trapdoor,
and
she
found
herself
in
a
cozy
cellar. The
same
thing
happened
the
next
day
with
the
second
daughter. On
the
third
day,
it
was
the
youngest
daughter's
turn. She
reached
the
hut,
cooked
food
for
everyone,
and
went
to
bed. To
her
surprise,
when
she
woke
up,
she
wasn't
in
the
hut
anymore! Instead,
she
was
in
a
beautiful
palace. A
prince
and
his
three
attendants
were
there
too. The
prince
explained
that
a
wicked
witch
had
cast
a
spell
on
him,
turning
him
into
an
old
man.

The
spell
could
only
be
broken
when
a
kind
woman
arrived,
showing
kindness
not
only
to
the
prince
but
also
to
the
animals. The
youngest
daughter
had
broken
the
spell
with
her
kindness. The
prince
and
the
animals
were
free! Grateful
for
her
goodness,
the
prince
asked
her
to
stay
in
the
palace,
and
they
all
lived
happily
ever
after. Moral:
Kindness
has
the
power
to
break
even
the
strongest
spells
and
bring
happiness
to
others. The
Glass
Chamber
Once
upon
a
time,
a
tailor
was
traveling
when
he
stumbled
upon
an
old
hut.

Tired
and
in
need
of
rest,
he
decided
to
spend
the
night
there. When
he
woke
up
the
next
morning,
something
amazing
happened! Right
in
front
of
his
eyes,
a
stag
and
a
bull
started
to
fight. Surprisingly,
the
stag
won
the
battle! After
the
fight,
the

stag
spoke
to
the
tailor
and
told
him
about
a
special
stone. The
stag
said
that
if
the
tailor
moved
this
stone,
he
would
discover
a
treasure. Excited
about
the
prospect
of
a
fortune,
the
tailor
agreed
and
moved
the
stone.

To
his
surprise,
the
ground
beneath
him
opened
up,
and
he
fell
into
a
grand
hall. In
the
hall,
he
found
a
glass
chamber
with
a
girl
inside. The
stag,
which
could
talk,
instructed
the
tailor
to
break
the
glass
chamber
and
free
the
girl. Following
the
stag's
advice,
the
tailor
broke
the
glass,
and
the
girl
was
set
free. The
girl,
once
imprisoned
in
the
glass
chamber,
shared
her
story
with
the
tailor. She
was
the
daughter
of
a
wealthy
man.

A
wicked
magician
had
asked
her
to
marry
him,
but
when
she
refused,
he
turned
her
brother
into
a
stag
and
trapped
her
in
the
glass
chamber. As
soon
as
they
stepped
out
of
the
chamber,
a
magical
transformation
occurred. The
stag
turned
back
into
a
man! Overjoyed,
the
tailor
and
the
girl
realized
they
had
a
special
connection. They
decided
to
get
married,
and
from
that
day
on,
they
lived
happily
ever
after. Moral:
Kindness
and
bravery
can
break
curses
and
lead
to
unexpected
happiness.

The
Ghostly
Gift
of
Love
Once
upon
a
time,
there
was
a
kind
couple
who
had
a
guest
staying
with
them. This
guest
had
a
peculiar
experience
one
midnight. He
saw
a
girl
entering
the
house! Oh,
how
frightened
he
was! But
when
he
told
the
owner
of
the
house,
they
said
they
didn't
see
any
girl. The
next
night,
the
guest
saw
the
same
girl
again. This
time,
she
was
digging

between
the
floorboards. The
guest,
feeling
scared,
went
to
tell
the
lady
of
the
house
about
what
he
had
seen. The
lady,
however,
had
a
different
explanation.

She
shared
that
the
girl
might
be
their
daughter,
who
had
passed
away
a
month
ago. The
mother
explained
that
their
daughter
had
received
some
money
and
wanted
to
give
it
to
a
poor
man. She
had
hidden
the
money
until
she
found
the
right
person
but
unfortunately,
passed
away
before
that. The
mother
believed
that
the
girl
might
have
returned
to
check
on
the
money. With
the
guest's
help,
they
followed
the
girl's
actions
and
found
the
money
hidden
between
the
floorboards,
just
as
the
guest
had
described.

Following
their
daughter's
wish,
the
parents
donated
the
money
to
a
poor
man. After
that,
the
girl
was
never
seen
again. The
parents
believed
that
she
was
at
peace,
knowing
her
wish
had
been
fulfilled. Moral:
Keeping
promises,
even
beyond
life,
can
bring
peace
and
happiness. The
Man
Who
Believed
He
Was
the
Smartest
Once
upon
a
time,
there
was
a
man
who
loved
to
boast. One
day,
he
proudly
told
his
friend
that
he
was
the
smartest
person
in
the
whole
wide
world! The
friend,
having
another
guest
with
him,
wasn't
so
sure.

The
guest,
hearing
the
bragging,
decided
to
challenge
the
man. He
said,
"Let's
see
who's
truly
clever. Come
back
tomorrow,
and
we'll
find
out!" The
next
day,
the
boastful
man
set
out
on
his
way. On
his
journey,
he
came
across
a
lovely
shoe
lying
on
the
path. However,
he
didn't
stop
to
pick
it
up. Little
did
he
know,
his
challenger
was
hiding
nearby. After
the
bragging
man
passed
by,
the
challenger
picked
up
the
shoe,
took
a
shortcut,
and
reached
a
spot
ahead
of
the
braggart. He
cleverly
placed
the
shoe
back
on
the
path
and
waited.

When
the
boastful
man
came
along,
he
was
surprised
to
see
another
shoe
that
looked
just
like
the
one
he
saw
earlier. Confused,
he
realized
he
should
have
picked
up
the
first
shoe. So,
he
decided
to
go
back,
leaving
his
sled
and
deer
tied
to
a
tree. As
he
retraced
his
steps,
the
challenger
picked
up
both
shoes
and
the
sled. Poof! He
vanished
from
the
spot. The
bragging
man
returned,
only
to
find
his
sled
missing! He
figured
out
what
had
happened
and
followed
the
footprints
of
his
deer
to
the
challenger's
house.

There,
he
admitted
his
defeat
and
went
home
without
his
sled,
as
a
reminder
not
to
boast
too
much. Moral:
it's
better
to
be
humble
than
to
brag,
or
you
might
end
up
losing
something
important.
